proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown vesting and disposal of remaining property
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 60(2) vests remaining holder property in the Crown, subject to agreements, and allows Minister disposal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when property remaining on a claim area vests in the Crown and may be disposed of.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuing liability after claim ends
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 60(3) keeps the former holder liable for obligations existing immediately before expiry, surrender, or cancellation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which obligations continue after a mineral claim ends.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Withdrawal of expired or surrendered claim area
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 60(4) withdraws the claim area after expiry or surrender for the period specified by the Recorder.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the withdrawal effect after expiry or surrender of a mineral claim.

proposals.reason: Section 61 covers notice of dispute filing, contents, service address, late filing limits, Recorder steps, and application of dispute provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Filing notice of dispute over mineral claim registration
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 61(1) and 61(2) allow a prospector to file a duplicate notice of dispute with the prescribed fee.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may file a notice of dispute and what must accompany it.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Claimed entitlement and address for service
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 61(3) and 61(4) require particulars if entitlement is claimed and an address for service.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what entitlement details and service address are required in a notice of dispute.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Late filing limits and Recorder steps
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 61(5) and 61(6) limit filing after 60 days and require the Recorder to note, retain, mail, and send the notice.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a late notice of dispute may be filed and what the Recorder must do after filing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application of dispute provisions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 61(7) applies sections 13 and 113 after section 61 requirements are met.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which provisions apply once notice of dispute requirements are met.

proposals.reason: Section 62 allows regional surveys to be credited toward required work and sets fifteen-year and five-year report deadlines plus regulation compliance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regional survey credits and reports
proposedGroups.reason: Section 62 allows regional surveys to be credited toward required work and sets fifteen-year and five-year report deadlines plus regulation compliance.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when regional surveys may be credited toward required work and when reports are due.

proposals.reason: Section 66 requires notice before unauthorized reduction of drill core or cuttings value, lists Recorder response options, allocates Crown expense, and creates a six-month non-response exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice and Recorder actions for intended drill core disposal
proposedGroups.reason: Section 66 requires notice before unauthorized reduction of drill core or cuttings value, lists Recorder response options, allocates Crown expense, and creates a six-month non-response exception.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice, Recorder action, Crown expense, and six-month non-response rules for drill core or cuttings.

proposals.reason: Section 68 is a detailed mining lease grant provision that should be split into eligibility, application submissions, environmental approval, survey exception, and conversion effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Eligibility and necessity for mining lease application
proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 68(1)(a), 68(1)(a.1), and 68(1)(b) require good-standing claims, whole claim units, mineral proof, and a production decision.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the claim status, land-unit, orebody, and production-decision conditions for obtaining a mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required application submissions and security
proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 68(1)(c) and 68(1)(d) require feasibility, corporate or partnership information, landowner or security proof, environmental security, mineral rights, fees, rent, and required work proof.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the information, proof, security, fee, rent, and required-work submissions for a mining lease application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Environmental program approval before lease grant
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 68(2) bars grant until the Minister approves the protection, reclamation, and rehabilitation program after obtaining specified approvals.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the environmental program approval condition before granting a mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Boundary survey exception and mineral claim replacement
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 68(3) and 68(4) address when another boundary survey is not required and when mineral claims are replaced by the mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prior-survey exception and the effect of the first mining lease term on mineral claims.

proposals.reason: Section 69 sets duplicate execution, filing and recording, attorney instrument filing, and Recorder certification on the counterpart.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Execution filing recording and certification of mining leases
proposedGroups.reason: Section 69 sets duplicate execution, filing and recording, attorney instrument filing, and Recorder certification on the counterpart.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how mining leases are executed, filed, recorded, and certified.

proposals.reason: Section 70 requires annual rent by anniversary date and reduces coal mining lease rent by prior-year royalty while preserving a minimum.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease rent and coal royalty reduction
proposedGroups.reason: Section 70 requires annual rent by anniversary date and reduces coal mining lease rent by prior-year royalty while preserving a minimum.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall annual rent timing and the coal royalty reduction rule for mining leases.

proposals.reason: Section 71 requires annual work statements and reports when not in production and applies mineral claim renewal provisions to mining leases with modifications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual mining lease work statement and report
proposedGroups.reason: Section 71 requires annual work statements and reports when not in production and applies mineral claim renewal provisions to mining leases with modifications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall annual work statement and report duties for mining leases not in production.

proposals.reason: Section 73 allows renewal for a further twenty-year term on written application at least six months before expiry, with up to two additional twenty-year terms.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease renewal timing and additional terms
proposedGroups.reason: Section 73 allows renewal for a further twenty-year term on written application at least six months before expiry, with up to two additional twenty-year terms.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when and how a mining lease may be renewed.

proposals.reason: Section 74 prohibits assignment or transfer of lease rights without written Minister consent and allows refusal in the public interest.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister consent required for mining lease assignment or transfer
proposedGroups.reason: Section 74 prohibits assignment or transfer of lease rights without written Minister consent and allows refusal in the public interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the consent requirement and public-interest refusal rule for mining lease transfers.

proposals.reason: Section 75 contains two separate mining lease topics: the operational rights granted to the lessee and the holder liability for damage or interference on the lease area.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease access, prospecting, mining and production rights
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 75(1) lists the rights a mining lease gives the lessee, including access, prospecting, mining, sampling, testing and production rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the access, prospecting, mining, sampling, testing and production rights granted by a mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease holder liability for damage or interference
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 75(2) separately states the holder liability for actual damage to or interference with use and enjoyment of property.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the holder of a mining lease is liable for damage or interference with property use and enjoyment.

proposals.reason: Section 76 separates immediate notice duties when production misses, drops or ceases from the Minister’s ability to require in-Province processing and the economic-ability limit on that requirement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice of delayed, reduced or ceased production
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 76(1) sets the production situations that trigger immediate notice to the Minister with reasons.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a lessee must immediately notify the Minister about production failure, reduction or cessation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister-required mineral processing in the Province
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 76(2) and 76(3) work together because one authorizes a processing requirement and the other limits it to cases where the lessee is economically able.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may require minerals mined under a lease to be processed or further processed in the Province.

proposals.reason: Section 77 is one opening or reopening workflow: advance notice and feasibility-study revisions must be submitted before production work begins, with approval required for environmental program revisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Opening or reopening mine notice and pre-work approvals
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the notice, revised feasibility particulars and approvals required before opening or reopening production work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice, revised feasibility particulars and approvals required before opening or reopening a mine for production.

proposals.reason: Section 80 is a focused reporting provision requiring lessees and lease holders to submit regulation-required returns and an annual work-and-minerals statement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease returns and annual work statement
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections concern returns or statements to the Recorder about work and minerals under a mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the returns and annual work-and-minerals statement required from lessees and mining lease holders.

proposals.reason: Section 84 contains one group of investigation and decision steps after alleged non-compliance, and a separate consequence group for cancellation and withdrawal of the lease land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister notice, investigation and decision after lease non-compliance
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 84(1) and 84(2) set the notice, minimum investigation timing, investigation, possible lease cancellation or extensions, and notice of decision.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Minister’s notice, investigation and decision powers after alleged mining lease non-compliance.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Lease cancellation after extended non-compliance and land withdrawal
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 84(3) and 84(4) state the mandatory cancellation after failure to comply within extended time and the resulting withdrawal of land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what happens when a lessee fails to comply within an extended time and how cancelled lease land is treated.

proposals.reason: Section 85 is one surrender-filing rule with a related substitute statement when the counterpart of the lease is lost or unavailable.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Surrender of mining lease and missing counterpart statement
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address how a lessee files a surrender and what may replace a lost or unavailable lease counterpart.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a lessee surrenders a mining lease and what replaces a lost or unavailable counterpart.

proposals.reason: Section 87 separates the former lessee’s one-year removal rights and limits from ownership rules for remaining property and extracted minerals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Former lessee one-year removal rights and limits
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 87(1) sets the one-year period for removing structures, equipment and minerals and identifies supports, timbers and framework that may not be removed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a former lessee may remove within one year after a lease expires, is surrendered or is cancelled.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ownership of property and extracted minerals left after the removal period
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 87(2) and 87(3) state who owns remaining structures, equipment, property and extracted minerals after the removal period expires.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who owns structures, equipment, property and extracted minerals left after the former lessee’s removal period expires.

proposals.reason: Section 98 is one royalty-liability rule with an exception where the person is liable for tax under the Metallic Minerals Tax Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining lease royalties and Metallic Minerals Tax Act exception
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections determine when a person who obtains or takes minerals under a mining lease must pay royalties and when the tax liability exception applies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who must pay royalties for minerals taken under a mining lease and when the Metallic Minerals Tax Act exception applies.

proposals.reason: Section 99 separates royalty payment due dates from the Lieutenant-Governor in Council power to suspend royalty requirements for better management of mines and minerals.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Royalty due dates for coal and other royalties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 99(1) sets monthly due dates for coal royalties and quarterly due dates for other royalties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when coal royalties and other royalties are due and payable.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Suspension of royalty payment requirements
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 99(2) separately authorizes suspending royalty payment requirements for up to ten years.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the requirement to pay royalties may be suspended and the maximum suspension period.

proposals.reason: Section 100 contains a collection framework with two teachable parts: interest/debt/action recovery and certificate-based judgment enforcement after default.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Interest, Crown debt and court action for unpaid royalties, charges or rent
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 100(1) to 100(4) address interest, Crown debt status, recovery by action and costs in that action.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how unpaid royalty, charge or rent amounts bear interest, become Crown debts and may be recovered by action.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister certificate and judgment enforcement after default
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 100(5) to 100(8) set the certificate, demand, filing, judgment and costs process after default.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a Minister certificate for unpaid royalty, charge or rent becomes enforceable as a Court judgment.

proposals.reason: Section 102 separates ordinary mining-lease instrument execution and consent requirements from a special filing rule for bank security instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Execution, authorization and Minister consent for mining lease instruments
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 102(1) and 102(2) set execution, verification, agent authorization and Minister consent requirements for instruments affecting a mining lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the execution, agent authorization and consent requirements before the Recorder receives a mining lease instrument.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Filing bank security instruments affecting mineral claims or mining leases
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 102(3) separately specifies what must be filed when a mineral claim, mining lease or interest is assigned or transferred as bank security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what must be filed with the Recorder for bank security affecting a mineral claim, mining lease or interest.

proposals.reason: Section 106 separates the authentication and evidentiary requirements for non-ordinary transfers from the Recorder’s duty to enter the entitled person in the records.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Statement, consent and evidence for death, bankruptcy, insolvency or other transfers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 106(1) and 106(2) state the verified statement, Minister consent for mining leases and supporting documents required for specified transfers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the statement, consent and evidence required for transfers by death, bankruptcy, insolvency or other non-ordinary means.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder entry of person entitled under transfer
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 106(3) separately directs the Recorder to enter the name of the person entitled under the transfer when the required materials are received.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what the Recorder must do after receiving the required transfer statement, consent and documents.

proposals.reason: Section 107 separates address information required on applications and transfers from the legal effect and substitution of addresses for service.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Address information required before filing or recording mining lease applications and transfers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 107(1) and 107(3) set the residence and post office address information required on applications, transfers and assignments before filing or recording.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the address information required before mining lease applications, transfers or assignments may be filed or recorded.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Address for service and substituted New Brunswick service person
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 107(2) and 107(4) to 107(6) address registered-mail service, substitution of a resident service person and the effect of service.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how address for service and substituted service persons work for mining rights notices, demands and proceedings.

proposals.reason: Section 108 contains three distinct topics: rights that claims or leases do not confer, duties to minimize injury and avoid interference, and Board cancellation for unauthorized land use.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rights not conferred by mineral claims or mining leases
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 108(1) to 108(3) list possession, surface-material and non-mineral-taking rights that a mineral claim or mining lease does not confer.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which possession, surface-material and non-mineral-taking rights are not conferred by a mineral claim or mining lease.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Least injurious land use and non-interference with other resource operations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 108(4) and 108(5) impose the least-injurious-use duty and prohibit interference with operations under specified Acts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the least-injurious-use duty and the non-interference rule for other resource operations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Board hearing, cancellation and withdrawal for unauthorized land use
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 108(6) and 108(7) provide for a Board hearing, cancellation and withdrawal where land is used for an unauthorized purpose.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how unauthorized use of claim, lease or mine land can lead to a Board hearing, cancellation and withdrawal.

proposals.reason: Section 109 is too broad for one unit because it covers private-property contact and permission, substitute routes when contact or agreement fails, environmental security, consent-protected lands, and repeat/exception rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Private-property contact, notice, agreement and Recorder permission before planned work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 109(1) to 109(3) state the default personal-contact path and alternatives where contact or agreement with the owner has not been achieved.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the private-property contact, notice, agreement, security and Recorder permission rules before planned work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Reclamation program, security, owner copy and waiting period for private-property work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 109(3.1) to 109(3.5) cover Minister-required reclamation programs and security, decision factors, delivery of the program to the owner, a sixty-day waiting period and written consent to earlier commencement.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when private-property work may require a reclamation program and security and what delivery and waiting-period rules follow.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Consent-protected lands for private-property damage or interference
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 109(4) lists lands where actual damage or interference cannot occur without the specified consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which private lands require specific consent before causing damage or interference with use and enjoyment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Staking exception and repeat requirements for planned work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 109(5) and 109(6) address the staking-only exception and when the notice and related steps must be repeated each year or after significant change.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the staking-only exception and when private-property planned-work steps must be repeated.

proposals.reason: Section 110 covers several distinct Crown Lands topics: notice and Recorder permission, Minister-required reclamation security, permanent structures and lessee consent, and timber-interest compensation with Board determination.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown Lands planned-work notice, Recorder permission and staking-survey exception
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 110(1) and 110(3) establish the notice and Recorder permission rule before damage or interference with Crown Lands and the exception for staking, grid lines and surveys.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Crown Lands notice and Recorder permission requirement and the staking, grid-line and survey exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Reclamation program, security factors and approval before Crown Lands work
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 110(2), 110(2.1) and 110(2.2) cover Minister-required reclamation programs and security, the factors for requiring them and the approval/security preconditions before work starts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when Crown Lands work may require a reclamation program and security and what must happen before work starts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Permanent structures and leased Crown Lands consent limits
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 110(4) and 110(5) separately restrict permanent camps or structures on Crown Lands and damage or interference with leased Crown Lands without lessee consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Crown Lands limits on permanent structures and on damage or interference with leased Crown Lands.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Timber-interest payments and Board determination
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 110(6) and 110(7) address payment for timber cut or damaged, Board determination of disagreements and application of hearing provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how timber-interest payments and disputes are handled when mining rights affect Crown Lands timber.

proposals.reason: Section 111 is a focused security rule: security compensates owners or lessees for damage or interference and must be deposited before prospecting, mining or other work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Security for damage or interference before work on land
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 111(1) and 111(2) explain what security compensates and when it must be deposited with the Recorder.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what section 111 security compensates and when it must be deposited before work on land.

proposals.reason: Section 112 gives one enforcement sequence for negotiable security: negotiate it after a non-payment certificate and require new security afterward.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Negotiating security after non-payment and replacing it
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address negotiating security to satisfy an unpaid amount and the following duty to deposit new security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when negotiable security is negotiated after non-payment and what replacement security is required.

proposals.reason: Section 113 is too broad for one unit because it covers initiating Board adjudications, summary or absent-party hearing powers, compliance and recording bars, and Court filing of Board orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Applying to the Board for adjudication and notice of application
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 113(1) and 113(2) address who may apply to the Board for adjudication and whom the Board must notify.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may apply for Board adjudication under the hearings Part and who must be notified.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Summary hearing, absence of party and time adjustments
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 113(6), 113(12) and 113(13) address summary hearings, proceeding when a notified party is absent and extending or abridging time.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Board’s summary-hearing, absent-party and time-adjustment powers in hearings.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Compliance with Board decisions and bar on recording or lease applications
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 113(9) and 113(10) require compliance with Board decisions and restrict recording claims or considering mining lease applications while Board matters or appeal periods are pending.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the compliance deadline for Board decisions and when land subject to Board proceedings blocks recording or lease applications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court filing and enforcement of Board orders
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 113(14) and 113(15) state how Board orders may be filed, entered and enforced as Court judgments with related costs.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Board orders are filed and enforced as Court judgments.

proposals.reason: Section 114 contains three distinct appeal-review topics: starting and supporting the review, the judge’s decision powers, and the Recorder bar while review is pending.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court review application, service, record, evidence and stay
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set the 30-day Notice of Application route, service, Board record delivery, evidence, stay and Rules of Court application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a party starts and supports a Court review of a Board decision or order and the stay effect of the application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Judge powers after hearing Court review application
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 114(6) and 114(7) state the judge’s powers to allow, dismiss or substitute a decision and to set an effective date after dismissal for certain Board decisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what a judge may do after hearing an application to review a Board decision or order.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder bar while land is subject to Court review
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 114(9) separately bars recording mineral claims and considering mining lease applications while the land is subject to a review application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a Court review application prevents recording a mineral claim or considering a mining lease application.

proposals.reason: Section 115 is a broad regulation-making provision with separate subject clusters for reporting and feasibility studies, registry and claim administration, mine operations and environmental controls, financial/offence machinery, and transitional or exemption powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations on returns, reports, feasibility studies and mine information

evidenceText: respecting returns, reports, plans, maps and statements
respecting the performance of feasibility studies

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 115(1)(a), (b), (g), (h), (i), (j), (k), (m) and (t) address operational reporting, feasibility, notices, mine operation, drill core, opening or closing mines, environmental work, confidentiality and dates.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers over mining reports, feasibility studies, operational notices, mine operations, environmental work, confidentiality and dates.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations on mineral claim registry, instruments and work commitments

evidenceText: registration of mineral claims in the registry
respecting instruments submitted to the registry
work commitment security deposit

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 115(1)(d) to (d.5) and (f) concern mineral claim registration, registry searches and support documents, instruments, effective changes, work commitment security and evidence of required work.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers over the registry, instruments, mineral claim changes, work commitments and evidence of work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations on fees, minerals, Board jurisdiction, security and prescribed lands

evidenceText: generally respecting fees
prescribing substances to be minerals
prescribing for purposes of section 13 matters
forms and amounts of security
prescribing lands and respecting consents

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 115(1)(l), (n), (o), (p), (q), (r) and (s.1) address fees, mineral classifications, Board jurisdiction, security, prescribed lands and forms or definitions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers over fees, mineral classifications, Board jurisdiction, security, prescribed lands, forms and definitions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations on offences, royalties, charges and rents

evidenceText: categories of offences
royalties, charges and rents payable
prescribing interest rates

proposedGroups.reason: Paragraphs 115(1)(r.1) and (s) address offence categories and royalties, charges, rents and interest rates.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation powers over offence categories and royalties, charges, rents and interest rates.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registry transitional regulations, retroactivity and specified non-application
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 115(1.1), 115(1.2) and 115(2) address transitional registry regulations, limited retroactivity and declarations that regulations do not apply to specified claims, leases or mines.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the transitional registry regulation power, its retroactivity limit and the power to declare non-application to specified mineral claims, leases or mines.

proposals.reason: Section 116 is a focused offence provision listing prohibited acts under the Act, with repealed paragraphs left as non-operative.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mining Act prohibited acts and failures to comply
proposedGroups.reason: The current operative subsection lists defacing or disturbing lawful marks, supplying false information, obstructing officials and failing to comply with Board decisions or orders.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the acts and failures that are offences under section 116.

proposals.reason: Section 117 is one non-interference offence rule, paired with a statement that prosecution does not replace civil liability.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Interference with another holder or operator’s mining
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the prohibition on unauthorized interference with another mining operation and the addition of prosecution liability to civil liability.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the prohibition on interfering with another holder or operator’s mining and how prosecution relates to civil liability.

proposals.reason: Section 122 is a coherent evidentiary rule for a Recorder certificate, including admissibility, notice to the opposing party and possible cross-examination.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recorder certificate evidence, notice and cross-examination
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections together address prima facie proof by certificate, pre-trial notice and requiring the Recorder’s attendance for cross-examination.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a Recorder certificate may be used as evidence and what notice and cross-examination rights apply.

proposals.reason: Section 123 separates the continuation or recording of previous-Act mining claims from special work, fee and excess-work credit treatment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Previous-Act mining claims deemed or recorded as mineral claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 123(1) and 123(2) state how recorded and staked-but-unrecorded claims under the previous Act become mineral claims under this Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how mining claims under the previous Act continue or may be recorded as mineral claims under this Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Work, fee and excess-work credits for previous-Act claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 123(3) and 123(4) preserve previous-Act work and fee rules for the term in progress and deem excess work credited with a tenth-term limit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how work requirements, fees in lieu of work and excess-work credits are treated for previous-Act mining claims.

proposals.reason: Section 124 is too broad for one unit because it covers continuation of previous-Act mining licences, conversion choices into leases or mineral claims, and credit, replacement and expiry consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuation and limited renewal of previous-Act mining licences
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 124(1) continues certain mining licences under the previous Act, applies previous-Act licence provisions and limits renewals to two one-year terms.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how previous-Act mining licences continue and how their renewal is limited.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Applying for mining leases or staking mineral claims before licence expiry
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 124(2) to 124(4.1) address the holder’s options or duties to apply for a mining lease, stake and record claims, and treat coal rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the lease-application, claim-staking and coal-right options or duties before a continued mining licence expires.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Credits, replacement, expiry and excess-work consequences for continued licences
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 124(5) to 124(9) cover work credits, replacement of the old licence, expiry consequences, coal withdrawal, deemed fifth term and excess-work carry-forward.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the work-credit, replacement, expiry, coal-withdrawal, term and excess-work consequences for continued mining licences.

proposals.reason: Section 125 is a focused saving rule continuing previous-Act mining leases and applying new-Act rent and required-work rules after renewal.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuation and renewal consequences for previous-Act mining leases
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address how previous-Act mining leases continue and what rent and required-work rules apply after renewal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how previous-Act mining leases continue and what rent and required-work rules apply after renewal.

proposals.reason: Section 126 is a coherent saving rule for withdrawn land and agreements, deeming previous-Act withdrawals and arrangements to continue under section 25 of this Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Previous-Act withdrawn lands and agreements deemed under section 25
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address land withdrawn under prior law and agreements, licences or leases that continue and are deemed under section 25.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how previous-Act withdrawn lands and related agreements, licences or leases continue under this Act.

proposals.reason: Section 133 is an amending provision, but it contains two discernible target topics: a substituted Metallic Minerals Tax Act definition of mining right and repeated office-name substitutions from director to mine assessor or Minister.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Metallic Minerals Tax Act mining right definition amendment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 133(1) repeals and substitutes the definition of mining right in the Metallic Minerals Tax Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the substituted Metallic Minerals Tax Act definition of mining right in this amending provision.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Metallic Minerals Tax Act director and mine assessor wording amendments
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 133(2) to 133(10) amend multiple provisions by repealing one subsection and substituting references to mine assessor, Minister or removing director wording.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the pattern of director, mine assessor and Minister wording changes made to the Metallic Minerals Tax Act.

proposals.reason: Section 135 is an amending provision for the Ownership of Minerals Act, focused on replacing mining-licence wording and preserving existing mining licences, leases, claims and rights from being affected by orders under that Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ownership of Minerals Act mining rights amendments
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections amend the Ownership of Minerals Act by changing wording about mining rights and replacing section 9 with a savings rule for specified mining rights.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Ownership of Minerals Act wording change and the replacement rule preserving specified mining rights.

proposals.reason: Section 137 only amends wording in the Security Frauds Prevention Act; the target is consequential amendment text rather than a self-contained Mining Act study rule.
Section 141 is commencement-only and contains no substantive study content beyond when the Act or section 140 comes into force.
Schedule A is an authoritative offence-category table linking specific Act provisions in Column I to Provincial Offences Procedure Act categories in Column II.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Schedule A Act offence categories

evidenceText: Column I
Column II
Category of Offence

proposedGroups.reason: The schedule functions as a table of offence categories for listed sections of the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that Schedule A maps listed Mining Act provisions to offence categories.

proposals.reason: Section 3 separates municipal corporate continuation or creation from territorial-limit continuation and inclusion of contiguous waterfront structures.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Corporate continuation and creation of municipalities
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 3(1) and 3(3) address existing cities and towns continuing as bodies corporate and newly created municipalities becoming bodies corporate.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how existing cities and towns continue and how newly created municipalities become bodies corporate.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal territorial limits and contiguous wharves, piers and similar structures
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 3(2) and 3(4) address continuation of territorial limits and inclusion of contiguous wharves, piers, docks, bridges, causeways, breakwaters and similar structures.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how territorial limits continue and how contiguous wharves, piers and similar structures are included within a municipality.

proposals.reason: Section 4 contains separate topics: corporate existence and general municipal powers, internal municipal organization and delegation, and recovery after a person defaults on a council direction.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal perpetual succession and general corporate powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 4(1) and 4(2) state perpetual succession and list general corporate powers to sue, contract, charge interest, hold property and take security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipality’s perpetual succession and general corporate powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal committees, departments and delegated administrative powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 4(3) separately authorizes municipal internal bodies and delegation of administrative powers and duties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipality’s power to create or alter internal bodies and delegate administrative powers and duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal action to recover expense and damages after default
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 4(4) separately allows council to cause a defaulted thing to be done and recover expense, costs and damages.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what council may recover when a person defaults on something lawfully ordered or directed by council.

proposals.reason: Section 5 is a coherent document-execution rule requiring a corporate seal and, except as provided by regulation, sealing and mayor-clerk signatures for municipal documents.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal corporate seal and document signing requirements
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the municipal seal and the sealing and signing requirements for agreements, contracts, deeds and other documents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the corporate seal and signing requirements for municipal documents.

proposals.reason: Section 7 separates municipal service authority and mandatory police protection from the powers to acquire land, enter service agreements and participate in natural gas or airport arrangements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal service authority, police protection and service administration
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 7(1) to 7(3) state which services may or must be provided and who administers, pays for and may make by-laws about them.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall municipal service authority, the police protection duty, and how service powers are administered and funded.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land acquisition and agreements for municipal services
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 7(4) separately authorizes acquiring adjacent land and entering agreements for shared costs, joint service arrangements and sewerage or water works.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the land acquisition and agreement powers a municipality may use when providing services.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Natural gas distribution and airport commission agreements
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 7(5) and 7(6) separately address agreements respecting natural gas distribution systems and airport commission participation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipality’s powers to enter natural gas distribution and airport commission agreements.

proposals.reason: Section 8 is a focused expropriation power with a clear boundary: municipalities may expropriate for services or powers, but not within another municipality or rural community.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal expropriation power and invalid cross-boundary expropriation
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections define the expropriation power and prohibit expropriation within another municipality or rural community.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a municipality may expropriate and when a purported expropriation is invalid.

proposals.reason: Section 9 is one council-authority rule vesting municipal powers in council and allowing a new council to continue proceedings begun by a previous council.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Council exercise of municipal powers and continuation of proceedings
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address council as the body exercising municipal powers and the continuity of proceedings between councils.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who exercises municipal powers and how a new council may continue previous council proceedings.

proposals.reason: Section 10 is a focused council-meetings rule setting the first-meeting timing after election and the minimum number of regular meetings each year.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: First council meeting timing and annual regular meetings
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address the clerk-fixed first meeting, the default fourth Monday of May meeting and the four-regular-meetings annual minimum.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the first council meeting is held after election and how many regular meetings council must hold each year.

proposals.reason: Section 11 combines a broad set of municipal by-law powers with a separate special-meeting rule limiting business to the notice unless unanimous consent is given.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal by-law powers for fees, licensing, retail operation, devices, signs, noise and tax collection

evidenceText: recreational or sports facilities
taxi cabs
retail businesses
transient traders
noise likely to cause a public nuisance

proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 11(1) lists by-law powers over recreational fees, taxi licensing, retail business on weekly day of rest, transient traders, guns and air rifles, exhibitions, amusement places, signs, vending machines, noise and tax collection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the main by-law powers listed in section 11 for municipal fees, licensing, retail operations, signs, devices, noise and tax collection.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Special meeting business limited to notice unless unanimous consent
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 11(2) separately restricts special-meeting business to what is specified in the notice unless all members present unanimously consent.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what business council may consider at a special meeting.

proposals.reason: Section 12 covers several distinct by-law passage rules: ordinary validity requirements, metric conversion revisions, official-language substitution by-laws, and meeting, amendment and voting mechanics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ordinary validity requirements for municipal by-laws
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 12(1) states the ordinary readings, publication alternative, seal, signature and enactment statement needed for a by-law to be valid.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the ordinary readings, publication alternative, seal, signature and enactment statement required for a valid municipal by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Metric-conversion by-law revision validity requirements
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 12(1.1) separately states validity requirements for a by-law revising measurements from Canadian units to the International System of Units.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the special validity requirements for a by-law that only revises measurements to International System units.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Official-language substitution by-laws and pre-third-reading amendment
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 12(1.2) and 12(1.3) address by-laws that substitute or add an official-language version and permit amendment before third reading without further filing.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the special validity and amendment rules for by-laws that substitute or add an official-language version.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: By-law readings, amendment before third reading, voting thresholds and saving rule
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 12(2) to 12(5) cover emergency readings, amendment before third reading, two-thirds or whole-council votes, meaning of whole council and protection of earlier by-laws.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the meeting, amendment, voting-threshold, whole-council and saving rules for passing by-laws.

proposals.reason: Section 14 is too broad for one unit because it covers Cabinet structural-change powers, who may institute or petition for proceedings, dissolution studies and limits, classification after changes, and regulation-making criteria.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Cabinet powers for incorporation, amalgamation, annexation, decrement and rural community conversion
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14(1) to 14(1.4) set the Lieutenant-Governor in Council’s structural-change powers, legislative or resolution requirements for amalgamations and contiguous-area grouping rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the Cabinet powers and consent or contiguity rules for municipal incorporation, amalgamation, annexation, decrement and rural community conversion.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Institution, petitions and studies for structural-change or dissolution proceedings
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify Minister, council, rural community council and resident petitions, interim council status after rural community incorporation, dissolution studies, special-Act dissolution limits and petition qualification dates.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may start or petition for municipal structural-change proceedings and how dissolution studies and petition dates work.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Incorporation as town, city or municipality after amalgamation or annexation
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 14(5) and 14(5.1) address incorporation as a town or city after amalgamation or annexation and mandatory incorporation after rural community amalgamation with municipalities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an amalgamated or annexed area may be incorporated as a town, city or municipality.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulations on conditions, procedures and criteria for structural changes
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 14(7) separately authorizes regulations respecting conditions, procedures and criteria for listed municipal structural changes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the regulation power over conditions, procedures and criteria for municipal structural changes.

proposals.reason: Section 19 is a long structural-change implementation provision with distinct topics for definitions, Order in Council contents, affected-municipality transition, first-council powers and finances, officer transition, information/time/conflict rules, and affected-area adjustments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Definitions for affected municipality and new municipality in structural-change orders
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(0.1) defines affected municipality, council of an affected municipality and new municipality for the section.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the definitions of affected municipality, council of an affected municipality and new municipality for structural-change orders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order in Council contents for incorporation, amalgamation, annexation or decrement
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(1) lists what an Order in Council may prescribe or provide, including name, boundaries, wards, planning designations, assets and liabilities, local commissions, first elections and incidental matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what an Order in Council may provide when effecting municipal incorporation, amalgamation, annexation or decrement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Affected council office, candidacy, day-to-day powers and void actions before effective date
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(2) to 19(5) address affected council terms, no by-elections, candidacy for first council, limits on affected council actions and voidness of contravening actions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how affected municipal councils and their members operate when a first election occurs before the effective structural-change date.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: First council appointments, transitional budget, advances and early by-law powers
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(6) to 19(8) address first-council officer appointments, transitional budget, procedure by-laws, new-municipality expense treatment and Minister of Finance advances.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the first council’s appointment, transitional budget, procedure by-law and advance-funding powers before the effective date.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: First council by-law review, estimates, collective agreements and officer transition
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(9) to 19(9.4) address by-law review, new by-laws, estimates, tax rate, collective agreements, officer appointments, officer revocation or reassignment, effective dates, voting threshold and service of resolutions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the first council’s powers over by-laws, estimates, collective agreements, officers and related resolutions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Information duties, time adjustments, conflict rules and affected-area adjustments
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 19(10) to 19(18) cover information requests, Minister time adjustments, conflict-of-interest protections, annexation or decrement without first election, affected-area planning and boundary adjustments, non-application rules and rural community application.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the information, time-adjustment, conflict, no-first-election, affected-area adjustment and rural-community application rules in section 19.

proposals.reason: Section 20 is a coherent by-law continuity rule for former municipalities after incorporation changes, amalgamation, annexation and decrement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuity or extension of former municipal by-laws after structural changes
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address which by-laws remain in force, extend to an annexed area or apply to a decreased municipality after structural changes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how by-laws continue, extend or apply after incorporation changes, amalgamation, annexation or decreased territorial limits.

proposals.reason: Section 21 is one assets-and-liabilities continuity rule for new municipalities and decreased territorial limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assets and liabilities after municipal structural changes
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address how assets and liabilities transfer to a new municipality or are adjusted when territorial limits decrease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how assets and liabilities of former municipalities and local commissions are treated after incorporation, amalgamation or decreased limits.

proposals.reason: Section 22 separates rescission and deemed village status for local improvement districts and named communities from the powers, services, assets and liabilities of the resulting villages.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rescission and deemed village status for local improvement districts and named communities
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 22(1) to 22(3.1) rescind incorporations, deem named entities to be villages and continue those villages until changed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which incorporations are rescinded and how the affected entities are deemed and continued as villages.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Powers, services, assets and liabilities of villages created under subsection 22(3)
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 22(4) addresses the powers and services the created village may carry out and the transfer of assets and liabilities from former entities within it.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what powers, services, assets and liabilities pass to a village created under subsection 22(3).

proposals.reason: Section 24 is too broad for one unit because it covers creating a local service district, meeting quorum and voting, repeat-petition and adjournment rules, later boundary changes or amalgamations, grouped annexations, service continuity and elector qualification dates.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Petition or Minister-initiated meeting to establish a local service district
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 24(1) to 24(4) set the petition or Minister-initiated process, boundary definition, meeting call, attendance threshold, majority decision, establishment power, one-year petition bar and adjournment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the petition, meeting, quorum, majority, one-year bar and adjournment rules for establishing a local service district.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Adding areas, annexing, amalgamating or changing local service district boundaries
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 24(5) to 24(6.2) address meetings for additions, annexations, amalgamations, boundary changes and grouped contiguous areas.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how local service district areas may be added, annexed, amalgamated or changed, including grouped-area contiguity.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Service continuity and elector qualification date after local service district changes
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 24(7) and 24(8) state that existing services continue after boundary changes unless discontinued and set the qualification date for electors.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how services continue after local service district boundary changes and which date determines elector qualifications.

proposals.reason: Section 25 has two major topics: meetings and decisions for adding or discontinuing local service district services, and the election, term and role of advisory committees.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Adding or discontinuing local service district services
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 25(1), 25(2) and 25(2.1) set the petition or Minister-initiated meeting process, attendance and majority thresholds, service addition or discontinuance and continuing liabilities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the meeting, quorum, majority and liability rules for adding or discontinuing local service district services.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local service district advisory committee election, term and role
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 25(3) to 25(8) address calling a meeting to elect an advisory committee, the election decision and size, name, four-year term, advisory role, new election meeting, combined meetings and elector qualification date.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a local service district advisory committee is elected, named, serves and assists the Minister.

proposals.reason: Section 27 separates local service district financing by real-property taxation from garbage and refuse service financing on a user-charge basis.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Taxation financing and different tax rates for local service district services
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 27(1) and 27(2) require the Minister to raise service money by taxation and allow different rates where service costs vary by area.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how money for local service district services is raised by taxation and when different area rates may be fixed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Garbage service user-charge financing and different user-charge rates
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 27(3) and 27(4) address raising garbage and refuse service money on a user-charge basis and fixing different user-charge rates where costs vary.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how garbage and refuse collection and disposal service may be financed by user-charges and varied by area.

proposals.reason: Section 28 separates default city and town council composition and by-law voting from notice, filing, election-timing and four-year amendment limits for composition by-laws.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: City and town council composition for municipalities without wards
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 28(1) and 28(1.1) state that a non-ward municipality council consists of a mayor and three or more councillors, and that composition by-laws require a majority of the whole council.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the default composition of a city or town council without wards and the vote needed for a composition by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice, filing, election timing and four-year limits for council composition by-laws
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 28(1.2) to 28(2) require public notice and posting before first reading, filing with the Municipal Electoral Officer, a six-month filing lead time for quadrennial elections and a four-year limit on amendment or repeal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice, filing, election-timing and four-year amendment limits for city and town council composition by-laws.

proposals.reason: Section 29 separates into ward-municipality council composition by by-law and Order in Council effects on that composition.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ward council composition by by-law
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set composition for ward municipalities and the by-law process for making, filing, and changing that composition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the mayor, ward councillor, councillor-at-large, vote, notice, filing, election timing, and four-year amendment rules for a section 29 by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order in Council council composition
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address composition set by an Order in Council and the four-year limits or approvals for a different by-law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an Order in Council affects council composition and when a later by-law may take effect or be approved.

proposals.reason: Section 31 separates ward division by by-law, Order in Council ward effects, and ward-resident voting.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ward division by by-law
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern continuing ward divisions, the by-law power, notice and filing, and election-period limits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how council may divide a municipality into wards by by-law and what notice, filing, and timing limits apply.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Order in Council ward division
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address ward divisions set by an Order in Council and the four-year effect of that division.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how an Order in Council ward division is deemed to operate and when a different by-law may be approved.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ward voters and ward candidates
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection is a distinct voting rule for ward candidates.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that only voters resident in a ward vote for candidates nominated for that ward.

proposals.reason: The target is repeal-only and contains no current operative content to author as a study unit.
Section 33 covers oath timing, oath administration and filing, and consequences or resignation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Oath timing for elected council office
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set when elected persons may or may not accept office by taking the oath.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall oath timing for accepting council office after quadrennial elections, by-elections, first elections, recounts, illness, and absence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Oath administration and filing
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover taking a seat, oath administrators, filing with the clerk, and minute recording.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who may administer the oath of office and how the oath is filed and recorded before a person takes a council seat.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Failure to take oath and resignation
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address failure to comply with the oath section and written resignation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the offence for failing to take the oath of office and how a council member may resign.

proposals.reason: The section coherently lists vacancy events and one non-vacancy rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Vacancy on council events
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections define vacancy-triggering events and the exception for increased council numbers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which events create a vacancy on council and when an increase in council size does not create a vacancy.

proposals.reason: Section 35 separates vacancy declaration and by-election duties from the twelve-month timing limit.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Vacancy declaration and by-election call
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify who declares vacancies and when the Municipal Electoral Officer holds a by-election.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who declares council vacancies and how declarations lead to a by-election.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Twelve-month by-election limit
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection gives a distinct timing restriction on by-elections before quadrennial elections.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a by-election is not held during the twelve months before a quadrennial election and the stated first-election exception.

proposals.reason: Section 36 covers distinct topics for mayor duties, deputy mayor replacement, councillor duties, and remuneration.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mayor duties and council control
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections list mayor duties and state that the mayor abides by council decisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the mayor duties and the rule that the mayor is subject to council direction and control.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Deputy mayor replacement of mayor
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection addresses absence, inability, vacancy, and substitute powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a deputy mayor acts in the mayor’s place and has the mayor’s powers and duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Councillor duties and remuneration
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections list councillor duties and authorize remuneration by by-law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall councillor duties and how council may provide salaries and expense allowances.

proposals.reason: The current operative content is election timing for quadrennial elections and first elections.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Quadrennial and first-election timing
proposedGroups.reason: The non-repealed subsections both address municipal election timing.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the quadrennial election date and the second-election timing rule after a first election near a quadrennial election.

proposals.reason: Section 39 separates ordinary tenure from resignation rules for members seeking another council office in a by-election.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Council member tenure
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection states how long a member of council holds office.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a council member holds office until the first meeting of the incoming council after a quadrennial election.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: By-election candidacy resignation
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover resignation-related candidacy limits, the twenty-one day resignation rule, and the Municipal Electoral Officer vacancy process.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when a council member must resign before seeking another council office in a by-election and how the resulting vacancy is handled.

proposals.reason: Section 68 separates plebiscite ordering and timing from vote-result and rural-community consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Plebiscite authority and timing
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize council to order a plebiscite and specify when it may be held.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the matters and timing for a municipal plebiscite.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Affirmative vote implementation and rural-community limits
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address the affirmative threshold, implementation duty, rural community application, and service-related limit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the sixty percent plebiscite implementation threshold and the rural community limits on service plebiscites.

proposals.reason: The section covers the effect of electing an ineligible person and the offence for sitting or voting while disqualified.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ineligible election and disqualified voting
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address consequences where a disqualified or incapable person is elected or participates on council.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that election of a disqualified or incapable person is void and that sitting or voting while disqualified is an offence.

proposals.reason: Section 74 separates officer appointment powers from tenure and dismissal protection.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal officer appointments
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify required and optional municipal offices and allow multiple offices in one person.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which municipal officers council must or may appoint and that one person may hold more than one office.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal officer tenure and dismissal
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections state tenure and dismissal-for-cause protection and one exception.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the tenure protection for full-time municipal officers and the section 19 resolution exception.

proposals.reason: Section 76 separates clerk duties from the assistant clerk substitute role.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Clerk meeting and record duties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 76(1) lists the clerk’s meeting, record, seal, notice, signing, and assigned duties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the clerk duties for council meetings, municipal records, by-laws, the seal, notices, documents, and assigned tasks.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assistant clerk powers and duties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 76(2) focuses on the assistant clerk’s direction and substitute powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an assistant clerk has the clerk’s powers and duties.

proposals.reason: Section 77 separates treasurer duties from the assistant treasurer substitute role.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Treasurer financial and accounting duties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 77(1) lists the treasurer’s chief financial and accounting duties.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the treasurer’s duties for municipal money, accounts, records, statements, insurance, advice, and assigned tasks.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assistant treasurer powers and duties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 77(2) focuses on the assistant treasurer’s direction and substitute powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an assistant treasurer has the treasurer’s powers and duties.

proposals.reason: The section is a focused municipal cheque signing rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal cheque signatures
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address cheque signatures and reproduced signatures.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who signs municipal cheques with the treasurer and when required signatures may be reproduced.

proposals.reason: Section 80 contains a solicitor qualification rule and a separate costs-recovery entitlement.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipal solicitor qualification
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection states who may be appointed or hold office as municipal solicitor.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipal solicitor must be a member of the Law Society of New Brunswick.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Municipality costs in actions
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection addresses the municipality’s entitlement to costs in actions and proceedings.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that a municipality may tax and collect lawful costs even where solicitor or counsel remuneration is paid by salary.

proposals.reason: Section 82 separates auditor qualification and audit duties from Minister cancellation and appointment powers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Auditor appointment and annual audit
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover qualification, duties, the March 1 deadline, and transmitting statements and report.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall auditor qualification, annual audit timing, and the duty to transmit certified financial statements and report to the Minister.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister cancellation and appointment of auditor
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address cancelling unqualified or incapable auditors and appointing an auditor when needed.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister cancels or appoints a municipal auditor and who pays the appointed auditor’s fees and expenses.

proposals.reason: Section 84 separates the bonding requirement and premiums from production, safekeeping, and reporting duties.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual bonding and premiums
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require annual bonding and municipal payment of premiums.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall that each municipality must provide annual bonding by by-law and pay the premiums for bonds.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Bond production safekeeping and report
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover bond production, safekeeping, and auditor reporting.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when bonds must be produced to council, how they are kept for auditor inspection, and what the auditor reports.

proposals.reason: The section addresses councillor eligibility for municipal appointment or employment and the volunteer exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Councillor eligibility for municipal employment
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections cover resignation, non-involvement, and voluntary employment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when an elected councillor is eligible for municipal appointment or employment and when volunteer employment is excluded.

proposals.reason: Section 87 contains fiscal-year, estimate, tax-base, rate-approval, and area-rate topics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Fiscal year and annual estimates
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set the fiscal year and annual estimate submission contents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the municipal fiscal year and what annual estimate, tax base, rate, tax imposition, and source information must be submitted.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown property municipal tax base
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address assessed value of real property owned by Canada.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Minister determines assessed value of Canadian Crown real property when computing the municipal tax base.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Assessment rate revision and approval
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections govern revised estimates, Minister approval, and failure to pass a resolution.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how estimates are revised after non-approval and how Minister approval fixes the rate for Real Property Tax Act purposes.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Different rates for municipal areas
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address service variation rates, annexed area rates, and adjustment to keep the estimate amount unchanged.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when different municipal rates may be fixed for different areas or annexed property and how the base rate is adjusted.

proposals.reason: The section covers public inspection of municipal documents with a closed-meeting exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Public inspection of municipal documents
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address available documents and closed meeting minutes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which municipal minutes, financial statements, estimates, and records are open to public inspection and the closed-meeting exception.

proposals.reason: Section 89 combines borrowing authority and limits with separate general-fund surplus and deficit adjustments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Current and capital borrowing limits
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover borrowing authority, limits, plebiscite authority, maximum constraints, net borrowing, and exclusions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall municipal borrowing authority and the current-operation, capital-expenditure, plebiscite, maximum, net-amount, and excluded-borrowing rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: General fund surplus and deficit adjustments
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address crediting surplus and debiting deficit to the current fund.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how audited general fund surplus and deficit are carried into the current fund for the second next ensuing year.

proposals.reason: Section 91 separates the amusement-device definition and licensing power from specific fees, confiscation, and regulation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Amusement device definition and licensing
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections define amusement device and authorize licensing.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what amusement device means and that council may provide for licensing of amusement devices by by-law.
